title: Giving a Voice to AI Agents: Scott Stephenson, CEO, Deepgram
talk_summary: Deepgram's CEO describes voice AI as a pipeline of speech-to-text, LLM, and text-to-speech stages, and argues the next step is passing rich context (audio, prior turns, embeddings, tone) between stages rather than treating each as independent. He also stresses right-sizing each component for cost-of-goods and keeping stages separate for controllability.

takeaways.technique: Pass structured context between pipeline stages
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of each stage seeing only its raw input, they feed prior-turn context and stage outputs (including embeddings and metadata like tone/speed) forward into the next stage.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it will take an audio and context so think prompt but not necessarily text prompt

takeaways.technique: Right-size each component in the stack
takeaways.what_they_do: Deliberately pick model size per stage: heavy compute where precision matters, small model where the task is narrow, expressive model only where output quality matters.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you choose the right size for each component in the stack

takeaways.what_they_do: They argue against collapsing everything into one monolithic model because separate stages give control over each part's behavior and cost.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the problem with putting them all together is it's not as controllable

takeaways.what_they_do: They note accuracy improves substantially when a model gets full conversation context versus a few seconds of it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what happens when you give that model the entire context of the conversation up until that point it gets way more accurate
